chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abbad ibn Suheyb who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a Christian who slandered a Muslim, so he said to him, 'O adulterer!' He said: 'He would be whipped eighty lashes due to the right of the Muslim, and eighty lashes except for one due to the sanctity of Islam, and his head would be shaved, and he would be paraded among the people of his religion so that others might be deterred.'

key_terms.قَذَفَ: Slandered (specifically in the context of hadd punishment)
key_terms.لِحَقِّ الْمُسْلِمِ: Due to the right of the Muslim
key_terms.لِحُرْمَةِ الْإِسْلَامِ: Due to the sanctity of Islam
key_terms.يَا زَانٍ: O adulterer (title used for the slanderer)
key_terms.يُنَكَّلَ: To be deterred/punished as an example

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for a Christian slandering a Muslim according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi details the distinct penal code for a Christian (Ahl al-Zimma) who slanders a Muslim, emphasizing the dual nature of the punishment: eighty lashes for the individual's right (haqq al-adam) and eighty minus one for the sanctity of Islam (haqq Allah). The inclusion of head-shaving and public parading within the Christian community serves as a specific deterrent (tanzeel), reflecting the Shia juristic view that non-Muslims under Muslim rule are subject to Islamic penal laws with certain contextual variations. This ruling underscores the principle of 'ta'abbud' (divine command) in hadd punishments while acknowledging the social dynamics of the dhimmi community.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abbad Bin Suheyb who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> was asked about a Christian who had slandered a Muslim, so he said to him, ‘O adulterer!’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He would be whipped eighty lashes due to a right of the Muslim, and eighty lashes except for one due to the sanctity of Al-Islam, and his head would be shaved off, and he would be paraded with among the people of his religion as a lesson for others’.
